 Philippines' 11.11 conversation gets a head start on Christmas shopping
 published

 author

 In the Philippines, the 11.11 shopping event served as more than an opportunity for eCommerce platforms to promote discounts. Brands also used the annual double-date sale to tap into the country's approaching Christmas shopping season, with holiday-themed messaging, giveaways and buy-now-pay-later promotions shaping the online conversation.
 Across social platforms, Shopee, Lazada and TikTok Shop competed for attention through mega-sale announcements, exclusive deals and limited-time offers. Their campaigns were accompanied by reminders to set alarms, join livestreams and participate in giveaways, while payment products such as SPayLater and TikTok PayLater gave shoppers another reason to engage with the sale.
 Meltwater recorded 4,585 mentions related to 11.11 in the Philippines between 11 October and 11 November 2026. This was considerably lower than Indonesia's 16,236 mentions over the same period, although the Philippine conversation also picked up towards the shopping date, rising from 136 mentions in the week of 12 October to 2,254 in the week of 9 November.
 Don't miss:  Brands take the lead as Indonesia's 11.11 conversation heats up 
 The conversation was notably more positive in tone than Indonesia's. Meltwater classified 53.1% of Philippine mentions as positive, compared with 44.9% neutral and 0.9% negative.
 A broader analysis by Tocanan, meanwhile, found a more balanced mix of promotional activity and consumer discussion. Of 6,052 relevant records captured between 1 and 11 November, 3,019 (49.9%) were classified as consumer discussion, compared with 2,637 (43.6%) promotional, brand or seller messages.
 The findings suggest that while promotional messaging helped shape the initial 11.11 conversation, shoppers were also discussing whether the offers represented genuine value. Price and value comparisons appeared in 3,305 records, or 54.6% of the analysed conversation, making it the most prominent topic.
 Platforms bring different propositions to the sale 
 Shopee led the Philippine 11.11 conversation among the major marketplaces, generating 969 mentions, according to Meltwater. Its activity included 11.11 sale promotions and SPayLater, which appeared in approximately 100 mentions.
 View this post on Instagram A post shared by Shopee Philippines (@shopee_ph) 
 Lazada followed with 750 mentions, with its mega-sale messaging and exclusive deals helping drive visibility. TikTok Shop recorded 646 mentions and stood out for its comparatively positive tone, with 71.2% of its mentions classified as positive by Meltwater.
 Its promotional activity included #tiktokshopph and #ttsgolden8pm, alongside TikTok PayLater, which appeared in approximately 70 to 80 mentions.
 The prominence of both SPayLater and TikTok PayLater points to how payment flexibility featured alongside discounts in the platforms' 11.11 messaging. Rather than focusing solely on price reductions, the platforms also brought their payment products into the shopping conversation.
 View this post on Instagram A post shared by TikTok Shop Philippines (@tiktokshop_philippines) 
 Shoppers, meanwhile, were comparing offers across marketplaces to determine where they could get better value.
 Tocanan's analysis captured examples of consumers revisiting products they had previously added to their carts and comparing prices across platforms. In one Reddit post, a shopper said a chair that had remained in their Shopee cart for five months was eventually purchased more cheaply on Lazada during the 11.11 sale.
 Beyond the marketplaces, Watsons emerged as another notable brand. It generated 115 mentions, with 95.7% classified as positive, the highest positive share among the individual brands highlighted in Meltwater's analysis.
 Its #watsons1111sale and #watsonsph campaigns, alongside promotions through the Watsons app, helped drive the conversation around the sale.
 Other brands also used the shopping occasion to promote their products and services. Honor Philippines highlighted devices including the Play 20A, Pad X7b and Magic V6, while Anytime Fitness used the event to amplify its #trainforyourlife messaging. GCash, Maybelline, Oxiglow, Bavin and Dermorepubliq also featured in the wider brand conversation.
 Christmas enters the 11.11 conversation 
 One distinction in the Philippine market was the connection between 11.11 promotions and the approaching holiday season.
 Meltwater found that terms such as 'holiday shopping' and 'holiday season' each appeared in approximately 80 to 100 mentions. This suggests that brands and sellers were positioning the shopping event within a broader period of gift-buying and seasonal preparation, rather than treating it as an isolated promotional date.
 View this post on Instagram A post shared by SPOT.ph (@spotph) 
 The holiday connection was also visible in shoppers' own discussions. Tocanan captured a shopper planning gifts for relatives within a budget of 300 pesos per person, while another post expressed the need to check out holiday gifts during 11.11 to take advantage of perceived savings.
 Brands also connected the event to practical seasonal needs. Lazada's promotional messaging positioned the sale as an opportunity to start Christmas gifting and home preparations, while foodpanda Philippines advertised discounts of up to 12% on Puregold groceries, framing 11.11 around household stocking-up.
 These examples suggest that the shopping event served different purposes, from finding affordable gifts to preparing for household needs, rather than focusing exclusively on discretionary purchases.
 Giveaways were another prominent feature of the conversation. Phrases such as 'reply to claim' and 'winners' appeared in approximately 170 and 121 mentions respectively, reflecting the use of comment-based participation and prize mechanics to encourage engagement, Meltwater said.
 Some sellers also took a more direct approach to social commerce. The top author identified by Meltwater, marasells, generated 170 mentions through posts using a reply-to-claim format to promote items described as being in mint condition.
 This illustrates how the 11.11 conversation extended beyond the official campaigns of major marketplaces. Individual sellers and promotional accounts also used the shopping event to bring product listings into social feeds and encourage direct interaction with prospective buyers.
 Promotional buzz meets shopper scrutiny 
 Despite the positive tone of the 11.11 conversation captured by Meltwater, the volume of promotional activity makes it difficult to establish how shoppers actually evaluated the sale.
 Meltwater found that businesses and brand accounts contributed more than half of the Philippine posts, although these accounts generated approximately 41% of total engagement. Among posts from other accounts, creator promotions were prominent. This points to the role of brands and creators in sustaining visibility around the shopping event, but does not necessarily indicate stronger purchase confidence.
 A broader analysis by Tocanan offers another perspective on the conversation. Of 6,052 relevant records captured between 1 and 11 November, 4,697, or 77.6%, were neutral in tone. Within the consumer-discussion subset, however, 387 records (12.8%) were positive, while 618 (20.5%) were negative and 62 (2.1%) were mixed.
 The findings captured both positive shopping experiences and frustrations with promotional offers. Some consumers reported securing products at prices they had been tracking, while others questioned whether discounts were worthwhile or found that advertised voucher prices could not be reproduced at checkout.
 In one example, a shopper said the price displayed after applying a voucher on a product page could not be obtained in the cart despite trying the available vouchers. This was an individual reported experience, rather than a verified pricing issue affecting the platform more broadly.
 Price and value discussions appeared in 54.6% of Tocanan's analysed records, while vouchers, coupons and promotional codes featured in 12.9%. This suggests that the mechanics behind an advertised discount were an important part of the shopping conversation, with consumers paying attention not only to the headline offer but also to the savings they could actually secure.
 Tocanan's analysis also identified 651 records classified as buying intent or consideration, alongside 345 completed-purchase self-reports within the consumer-discussion subset. These are individual records rather than unique buyers or verified transactions, but offer a more detailed picture of the behaviours surrounding the sale.
 For marketers, the findings highlight the importance of making promotional benefits easy to understand and reproduce at checkout. Clear voucher eligibility, minimum-spend requirements and credible comparison prices can help close the gap between the savings advertised and the value shoppers ultimately experience.
 Ultimately, promotional visibility and engagement are only part of the picture. As brands move from the 11.11 sale towards the Christmas shopping period, the more meaningful measure will be whether these interactions translate into sustained consumer consideration and purchases.
